idiom_name: Record<Op, Rule> over a discriminated token union + binding-power loop
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds exhaustiveness to the JavaScript idiom: a discriminated union of token types plus Record<Op, Rule> makes the compiler reject a table that forgets a new operator, and the loop is the same while-over-binding-power, with handler closures over the parser. TypeScript's own compiler uses the neighbouring technique for its grammar - parser.ts imports getBinaryOperatorPrecedence and OperatorPrecedence and climbs precedence explicitly - so the ecosystem precedent is the same family of hand-written precedence parsing, and nothing in the platform parses your DSL. Use the typed table while the operator set is small and growing; adopt a framework (Chevrotain, Peggy, nearley) when the language is large, needs grammar tooling, or must report errors like a compiler.
pitfalls: Record<Op, Rule> guarantees a row per operator, but the non-null assertions on nud/led hide missing handlers; make each row's handler requirements explicit or validate the table at startup.

The ?? 0 fallback treats an unknown token as "no binding power" and silently ends the expression; type the lookup so unknown tokens are impossible, or branch on the discriminated union and report the position.

Long chains recurse once per operator on the Node/V8 stack, so a depth guard keeps the failure a parse error instead of a RangeError - and type erasure means a token's claimed kind is only as trustworthy as the lexer that produced it.
